recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Future changes should use a separate terminology/THO or PA tracker if the encounter-participant-type value set content needs additional work; FHIR-9269 itself is already correctly reflected in current source.
issue_request: FHIR-9269 asked that ParticipationType bindings in Appointment and AppointmentResponse be loosened from required. Although the description said preferred, the accepted PA resolution says Appointment.participant.type and AppointmentResponse.participantType should be extensible, not required.
initial_application: Commit 4e7bd447d5bcd34260526609d8337e3c9108ca8e names tracker 9269 and added `Conformance = extensible` for the ParticipantType binding in both historical Appointment and AppointmentResponse spreadsheets. The later R4B StructureDefinition XML migration preserved `strength value="extensible"` for both elements.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Appointment and AppointmentResponse as active resources. Later same-area decisions do not contradict FHIR-9269: FHIR-34141 resolved no-change on expanding encounter-participant-type, and FHIR-53174 later relied on Appointment.participant.type already being extensible while adding explanatory text for location roles. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting FHIR-9269 discussion.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no source edit is needed: source/appointment/structuredefinition-Appointment.xml and source/appointmentresponse/structuredefinition-AppointmentResponse.xml already bind the relevant elements to encounter-participant-type with extensible strength.
